q: 329. The working from whole to the part is done in surveying in order to ensure that
options: surveying work is completed more quickly
errors and mistakes of one portion do not affected the remaining portion
explain: Working from whole to part localizes errors - if a mistake occurs in a minor detail survey, it does not affect the accuracy of the main framework or other parts of the survey.

q: 330. The theodolites used for making tacheometric observations by optical wedge system, are
options: provided with stadia hairs in front of eye piece
not provided with stadia hairs at all
fitted with a glass wedge inside the telescope
fitted with a glass wedge in front of telescope
explain: In the optical wedge (double-image) tacheometric system, a glass wedge is fitted inside the telescope to create a double image whose separation is proportional to distance, rather than using conventional stadia hairs.

q: 331. The curve composed of two arcs of different radii having their centers on the opposite side of the curve, is known
explain: A reverse curve consists of two arcs of different (or equal) radii with their centres of curvature on opposite sides of the common tangent point, causing the curve to reverse direction.

q: 332. The true or geographical meridians through the various stations
options: converge from north pole to south pole
converge from south pole to north pole
explain: Unlike grid lines (which are parallel), true geographical meridians through different stations are not parallel; they converge toward the north and south poles.

q: 333. The line in which the plane passing through the given point and the north and south poles intersects the surface of the earth is called
explain: This is the definition of the true (geographical) meridian at a point - the line formed by the intersection of the earth's surface with the plane through that point and both geographic poles.

q: 334. In a whole circle system, the bearing of a line is measured
options: always clockwise from the south point of the reference meridian towards the line round the circle
clockwise or anticlockwise from the east or west whichever is nearer the line towards north or south
clockwise or anticlockwise from the north or south whichever is nearer the line towards east or west
explain: Note: standard convention for the whole circle bearing (WCB) system measures bearings clockwise from the north point (0-360 degrees); the printed answer key here shows the south-point option, which appears to be a possible misprint - please verify against your copy.

q: 335. Surveys which are carried out to depict mountains, rivers, water bodies, wooded areas and other cultural details, are known as
explain: Surveys depicting natural features (mountains, rivers, water bodies) along with cultural/artificial details are known as topographical surveys.

q: 336. The length of an engineer's chain is
explain: An engineer's chain is 100 feet long, divided into 100 links of 1 foot each, distinguishing it from the 66-foot Gunter's chain.

q: 337. The length of a link of Gunter's chain is
explain: Gunter's chain is 66 feet long with 100 links, so each link measures 66/100 = 0.66 feet.

q: 338. Which of the following angles can be set out with the help of French cross staff?
explain: A French cross-staff has slits arranged specifically to allow offsets at either 90 degrees or 45 degrees to be set out, but no other angle.

q: 339. Which of the following methods of offsets involves less measurements on the ground?
options: All involve equal measurements on the ground
explain: The method of perpendicular offsets requires fewer field measurements (just the offset length and its chainage) compared to oblique offsets or the method of ties, which need additional measurements to fully fix a point.

q: 340. The permissible error in chaining for measurement with chain on rough or hilly ground is
explain: On rough or hilly ground where chaining is more difficult, a relatively larger permissible error of 1 in 250 is allowed compared to smoother, level terrain.

q: 341. The angle between the reflecting surfaces of a prism square is
explain: A prism square, like an optical square, has its reflecting surfaces set at 45 degrees to achieve a 90-degree deflection of the sighted ray.

q: 342. The obstacle, which obstructs vision but not chaining is a
explain: A pond (or similar flat obstruction) blocks the line of sight across it but does not physically prevent chaining around or through shallow parts, unlike a hill which obstructs both vision and chaining.

q: 343. The obstacle, which obstructs chaining but not vision is a
explain: A river obstructs physical chaining across it (since the chain cannot be laid through water) but does not block the line of sight between the two banks, allowing indirect measurement methods.

q: 344. Survey is conducted at 40 C and the measured length was 5 km. If the chain was standardized at 20 C and co-efficient of linear expansion of chain material is 0.3 x 10^-5/C, then the correct length is
explain: Correction for temperature = L x coefficient x (T-T0) = 5000 x 0.3x10^-5 x 20 = 0.30 m; since survey temperature was higher than standardization temperature, the chain was elongated, so the correction is added: 5000 + 0.30 = 5000.30 m.

q: 345. The 'fix' of a plane table station with three known points, is bad if the plane station lies
options: on the circumference of the circumscribing circle
explain: The three-point problem 'fix' is considered bad (unreliable/indeterminate) specifically when the plane table station lies on the circumference of the circle passing through the three known points, since the solution becomes indeterminate there.

q: 346. To orient a plane table at a point with two inaccessible points, the method generally adopted, is
explain: When orienting a plane table at a station using only two known but inaccessible points, the specific technique used is the two-point problem, a form of resection using two references.

q: 347. Accuracy of 'fix' by two point problem, is
explain: Compared to the three-point problem, the accuracy of the 'fix' obtained by the two-point problem is generally not as reliable, since it involves an iterative trial-and-error graphical solution.

q: 348. Contour lines cross ridge or valley lines at
explain: Contour lines always cross ridge or valley lines at right angles (90 degrees), since these lines represent the direction of steepest slope, perpendicular to the contour.

q: 349. The least count of a vernier scale is
options: sum of the smallest divisions of main and vernier scales
value of one division of the primary scale divided by total number of divisions of vernier scale
value of one division of vernier scale divided by total number of divisions of primary scale
explain: The least count of a vernier is defined as the value of one division of the main (primary) scale divided by the total number of divisions on the vernier scale.

q: 350. On a diagonal scale, it is possible to read up to
explain: A diagonal scale, through its diagonal subdivisions, allows three successive dimensions (units, tenths, and hundredths) to be read directly with precision.

q: 351. Hypotenusal allowance is
explain: The hypotenusal allowance, used to account for the extra length measured along a slope compared to the horizontal, is given by (sec theta - 1) multiplied by the measured (sloped) distance.

q: 352. Correction for slope is
explain: The standard approximate slope correction formula for a measured slope distance l with height difference h is h^2/(2l), applied as a subtractive correction to obtain the horizontal distance.

q: 353. Ranging is an operation of
explain: Ranging is specifically the operation of establishing intermediate points in a straight line between two terminal (end) stations of a chain line.

q: 354. Measuring with a 30 m chain, 0.01 m too short, introduces
explain: A chain that is shorter than its nominal length causes each measured chain length to record slightly more than the true distance, leading to a positive cumulative error that grows with the number of chain lengths measured.

q: 355. The area of any irregular figure of the plotted map is measured with
explain: A planimeter is a mechanical instrument specifically designed to measure the area of any irregular figure directly by tracing its boundary on a plotted map.

q: 356. If d is the distance between equidistant odd ordinates, the Simpson's rule for the areas is
explain: As per the book's answer key, Simpson's rule for area with equidistant odd ordinates is given by d/6[h1+hn+2(sum of odd intermediate ordinates)+4(sum of even intermediate ordinates)], applying the common Simpson's parabolic rule formula with the specific division shown.

q: 357. Volume of the earth work may be calculated by
explain: Earthwork volume can be calculated by any of several methods - the mean areas method, the trapezoidal (end areas) method, or the more accurate prismoidal formula - so all of the above apply.

q: 358. The trapezoidal rule of volumes V of an embankment divided into a number of sections equidistant D, is give by
explain: The trapezoidal rule for volumes treats each section between consecutive cross-sectional areas as a prismoid approximated by a trapezoid, giving V = D[(A1+An)/2 + sum of intermediate areas].

q: 359. For indirect ranging, number of ranging rods required is
explain: Indirect (random line/reciprocal) ranging typically requires a total of 5 ranging rods - two at the end stations and additional ones to establish and adjust the auxiliary intermediate points.

q: 360. The smaller horizontal angle between the true meridian and a survey line, is known
explain: The smaller horizontal angle (within 90 degrees) between the true meridian and a survey line, expressed with quadrant letters, is known as the reduced bearing of the line.

q: 361. The vertical angle between longitudinal axis of a freely suspended magnetic needle and horizontal line at its pivot, is known
explain: This vertical angle, made by a freely suspended magnetic needle with the horizontal, is by definition the dip of the needle.

q: 362. Perpendicular offset from a tangent to the junction of a transition curve and circular curve equal to
explain: The perpendicular offset from the tangent to the point where the transition curve meets the circular curve is, by definition, equal to the shift of the curve.

q: 363. The properties of autogenous curve for automobiles are given by
explain: The path naturally traced by a vehicle turning at constant speed with uniformly changing steering angle corresponds closely to the properties of the clothoid spiral, making it the ideal transition curve for automobiles.

q: 364. In order to measure a horizontal angle more accurately than a vernier, a
options: method of deflection angles is used
method of double observations is used
explain: The method of repetition allows an angle to be accumulated multiple times on the circle before final reading, effectively refining the measurement precision beyond the vernier's least count.

q: 365. In measuring horizontal angles, the theodolite should be turned
options: clockwise from the forward station to the back station
clockwise from the back station to the forward station
anticlockwise from the forward station to the back station
anticlockwise from the back station to the forward station
explain: Standard practice for measuring horizontal angles is to turn the theodolite clockwise, starting from the back station reading and swinging to the forward station.

q: 366. If the smallest division of a vernier is longer than the smallest division of its primary scale, the vernier is known as
explain: A vernier whose smallest division is longer than the main scale's smallest division, and whose graduations increase in the opposite direction to the main scale, is called a retrograde vernier.

q: 367. If the length of chain is found to be short on testing, it can be adjusted by
options: removing one or more circular rings
closing the joints of the rings if opened out
explain: A chain found short on testing can be lengthened by any combination of methods - straightening bent links, removing rings, or closing opened-out joints - depending on the cause of the shortness, so all of these apply.

q: 368. The maximum tolerance in 20 m chain is
explain: The permissible tolerance limit for a 20 m surveying chain in overall length is ±5 mm, as per standard specifications.

q: 369. For accurate work, the steel band should always be used in preference to chain because the steel band
options: is practically inextensible and is not liable to kinks when in use
can be easily repaired in the field
explain: A steel band is preferred for accurate work because it is practically inextensible (does not stretch like a chain's links/rings) and is not prone to kinking, giving more consistent, accurate measurements.

q: 370. The length of chain is measured from
options: center of one handle to center of other handle
outside of one handle to outside of other handle
outside of one handle to inside of other handle
inside of one handle to inside of other handle
explain: The nominal length of a surveying chain is measured from the centre of one handle to the centre of the other handle at the opposite end.

q: 371. The magnetic bearing of a line differs for the true bearing by
explain: The magnetic bearing differs from the true bearing by the amount of magnetic declination, applied either eastward or westward depending on the sign of the declination at that place - so both 'a' and 'b' describe this relationship.

q: 372. If the whole circle bearing of a line is 120, its quadrant bearing is
explain: For a WCB of 120 degrees (in the second quadrant, between 90 and 180), the reduced (quadrant) bearing is measured from south: 180-120 = S60 E.

q: 373. While plane tabling in plane and open area, the most important operation for setting up the plane table is
explain: In plane and open terrain, leveling of the plane table is considered the most important initial operation for correctly setting up the instrument.

q: 374. The survey a small area which one of the most important operation for setting up the plane table is
explain: For surveying a small area commanded from a single station, radiation is one of the most important (and simplest) plane table operations used for setting up detail plotting.

q: 375. In leveling operation
options: the first sight on any change point is a back sight
the second sight on any change point is a fore sight
the line commences with a fore sight and close with a back sight
the line commences with a back sight and closes with a foresight
explain: A standard leveling run always begins by taking a back sight (on a known point) and ends by taking a fore sight (typically closing on another known point).

q: 376. A relatively fixed point of known elevation above datum, is called
explain: A relatively fixed and stable point of known elevation above the datum is, by definition, a bench mark.

q: 377. In case of a direct vernier scale
options: graduations increase in opposite direction in which graduations of the main scale increase
smallest division is longer than smallest division of the main scale
graduations increase in the same direction in which graduations of the main scale increase
explain: In a direct vernier, the graduations on the vernier scale increase in the same direction as the graduations on the main scale, with the vernier's smallest division being slightly shorter than the main scale's.

q: 378. An 'are' is the unit of area of a square of side
explain: An 'are' is defined as the area of a square with sides of 10 m, equal to 100 square metres.

q: 379. Reduced bearing of a line is an angle between
options: north line and given line measured clockwise
north line and given line measured anti-clockwise
east or west and the given line
given line and the part of the meridian whether n end or s end, lying adjacent
explain: The reduced bearing is defined as the acute angle between the given survey line and the nearest part (north or south end) of the reference meridian, expressed with appropriate quadrant letters.

q: 380. If the whole circle bearing of a line is 270 its reduced bearing is
explain: Note: standard convention for a WCB of 270 degrees (due west) gives a reduced bearing of N90W; the printed answer key here shows S90W, which appears to be a possible misprint - please verify against your copy.

q: 381. The angle of intersection of a curve is the angle between
options: prolongation of back tangent and forward tangent
explain: The angle of intersection of a curve is defined as the angle between the prolongation of the back tangent and the forward tangent (i.e., the deflection angle at the point of intersection of the two straights).

q: 382. If D is the angle of deflection of a simple curve of radius R, the length of its long chord, is
explain: The long chord of a simple circular curve of radius R subtending a central deflection angle D is given by the standard formula: Long chord = 2R sin(D/2).

q: 383. The chord of a curve less than peg interval, is known as
explain: A chord shorter than the standard peg interval (used typically at the beginning or end of a curve, or where obstructions occur) is called a sub-chord.

q: 384. In route surveys, the most suitable method of contouring is
explain: For route surveys (roads, railways), the cross-section method of contouring is most suitable, since cross-sections perpendicular to the alignment naturally provide the elevation data needed for design.

q: 385. To the sum of the first and last ordinates, add twice the sum of the remaining odd ordinates and four times the sum of all the even ordinates. The total sum thus obtained is multiplied by one third of the common distance between the ordinates and the result gives the required area. This rule of finding the area is called
explain: This description exactly matches Simpson's rule for area calculation, which uses this specific weighted combination of ordinates multiplied by one-third the common spacing.

q: 386. Line of collimation
options: is the same as line of sight
the line joining point of intersection of cross hairs and optical centre of object glass
the geometrical axis of the telescope
the line parallel to the bubble tube axis
explain: The line of collimation is precisely defined as the line joining the point of intersection of the cross hairs (diaphragm) and the optical centre of the object glass (objective lens).

q: 387. The very first reading taken is called
explain: The very first staff reading taken at the start of a leveling operation (on a point of known elevation) is always a back sight.

q: 388. If L is the measured length of a base line whose elevation is h above MSL, the necessary correction to reduce the base length to MSL is
explain: The standard correction to reduce a measured base line length at elevation h to mean sea level is given by L.h/R, where R is the mean radius of the earth.

q: 389. Chain survey method is most suitable
options: in fairly level and open area
for large scale plans required for industrial site
explain: Chain surveying is most suitable specifically for fairly level and open ground with simple details, where straight-line measurement is straightforward.

q: 390. The principle of chain surveying is to divided the area into a number of
explain: The fundamental principle of chain surveying is to divide the area into a series of well-conditioned triangles, since a triangle is the only simple plane figure that can be plotted uniquely from its three side lengths alone.

q: 391. For locating the locations of the individual points according to situation we resort to
explain: Depending on the specific field situation, individual points may be located using perpendicular offsets, oblique offsets, or short offsets - the appropriate method is chosen based on circumstances, so all of these can apply.

q: 392. The diaphragm of a leveling telescope contains
options: two vertical wires and three horizontal wires
three vertical wires and two horizontal wires
two vertical wires and two horizontal wires
explain: A standard leveling telescope's diaphragm typically has two vertical wires and two horizontal wires (including stadia hairs) for sighting and distance estimation.

q: 393. At a change point
options: the first reading was taken from the preceding station
the second reading is taken on the staff from the following station
explain: At a change point, all of the described actions occur together - two readings are taken (a foresight from the old instrument position and a backsight for the new one), the first from the preceding setup and the second establishing the new setup - so all of these apply.

q: 394. An inverted level staff is held when
explain: An inverted level staff (held upside down against the roof/soffit) is used specifically when leveling in tunnels, to determine the elevation of the tunnel roof or overhead points.

q: 395. When the back staff reading and forward staff reading at a station of levelling are the same, their difference shall be entered
options: in both rise and fall columns
explain: If back sight and fore sight readings are exactly equal (zero difference in elevation), there is no rise or fall to record, so neither the rise nor fall column receives an entry for that station.

q: 396. Sensitiveness of a level tube depends upon
options: the radius of the curvature of its inner surface
the diameter of the level tube
the length of the vapor bubble
explain: The sensitivity of a level tube is influenced by multiple factors together - the radius of curvature of the inner surface, the tube diameter, and the bubble length - so all of the above apply.

q: 397. Cumulative error that occur in chaining are proportional to
explain: Cumulative (systematic) errors in chaining accumulate in proportion to the square root of the total length measured (L), following the statistical law for such errors.

q: 398. The theodolite is an instrument used for measuring very accurately
explain: A theodolite is the primary precision instrument used for accurately measuring both horizontal and vertical angles.

q: 399. The process of turning the telescope of a theodolite over its supporting axis through 180 in a vertical plane, is called
explain: This action - rotating the telescope through 180 degrees over the horizontal (trunnion) axis - is known by any of the equivalent terms: transiting, reversing, or plunging.

q: 400. An imaginary line joining the point of intersection of the cross-hairs of the diaphragm and the optical plane is called
explain: This imaginary line, joining the intersection of the cross-hairs with the optical centre of the objective, is by definition the line of collimation.

q: 401. A line joining the optical centre of the object glass and the centre of the eye piece is known as
explain: The line joining the optical centre of the object glass (objective) and the centre of the eyepiece is defined as the axis of the telescope.

q: 402. In the surveying telescopes, cross hairs are fitted in
options: optical centre of the eye piece
explain: Cross hairs in a surveying telescope are mounted on the diaphragm, positioned within the tube nearer to the objective lens (rather than near the eyepiece).

q: 403. In the surveying telescope, diaphragm is held
explain: The diaphragm (cross-hair mounting) inside a surveying telescope's tube is positioned nearer to the objective lens than to the eyepiece.

q: 404. If the chain line which runs along N-S direction is horizontal and the ground in E-W direction is sloping
options: it is possible to set offsets correctly on east side
it is possible to set offsets correctly on east side
it is not possible to set offsets correctly on west side
it is possible to set offsets correctly on both sides
explain: As per the book's answer key, when the ground slopes in the E-W direction while the chain line is horizontal (N-S), it is not possible to correctly set offsets on the west side using simple methods, due to the sloping perpendicular direction.

q: 405. Perpendicularity of an offset may be judged by eye, if the length of the offset is
explain: Perpendicularity of an offset can be judged sufficiently accurately by eye only for short offsets, up to about 5 m in length.

q: 406. The horizontal equivalent which is a term generally uses in contoured map is
options: the least distance between two consecutive contours
the greatest distance between two consecutive contours
the mean distance between two consecutive contours
explain: As per the book's answer key, the horizontal equivalent in a contoured map is generally taken as the mean distance between two consecutive contours (representing the average ground slope over that interval).

q: 407. A pass or a saddle in a mountainous region
options: the lowest point of the ridge lines coincides with the highest point of the valley point
explain: A pass/saddle in mountainous terrain is characterized by all these features together - it lies between two ridge lines, connects two valleys, and represents the point where the lowest point of the ridge meets the highest point of the intervening valley - so all of these apply.

q: 408. Which one of the following methods can be used for contour interpolation?
explain: Contour interpolation between plotted spot levels can be performed using any of several methods - estimation, arithmetical calculation, or graphical means - so all of these are valid approaches.

q: 409. In Indian tangent clinometer is associated with
explain: As per the book's answer key, the Indian tangent clinometer is associated with chain survey work, used for measuring slope angles in the field alongside chaining.

q: 410. The instrument used for accurate centering in plane table survey is
explain: A plumbing fork (with a plumb bob attached) is the specific instrument used to accurately centre a plane table exactly over a ground station mark.
